cells.tense: You are here with what began as possibility and now has weight, and you stay with it.
cells.ask: Write one line naming the thing as done, set a date to stop it, and keep the date.
cells.core:
You know what you built, and you keep it in the open. What started as a maybe now has real weight, and you pick it up without complaint. When it comes up, you say what it took and what it cost. That plainness is why the ending you make next will hold its shape.

The weight is heavy because it is real. Keep it right by looking at it without flinching — one line that says this is done, one date that says when it stops. The direction is yours because you choose it, not because the load forces your hand. What you take on after this starts from that same plain sentence.
cells.sheetLine: You carry what you finished, honestly, and that is why it holds.
cells.place: at the ending that clears the ground for what comes after

cells.tense: You are out ahead of this ending, rehearsing a settled version while the present one sits unwatched.
cells.ask: Stop and describe one thing you can actually see about it right now, with no plan attached.
cells.core:
You keep reaching for the far side of this, for the cleared ground, for the version where it is behind you. So the last stretch gets run hard. Each step becomes proof that it is nearly finished, and you are somewhere ahead of your own feet. What you are carrying is already whole; the thing that is rushing is you.

Let one look land with no next step riding on it. The ending will arrive when it arrives; bracing does not pull it forward. The grip you are holding is not the weight, it is your picture of what comes after. Set the picture down and see what the thing looks like from here.
cells.sheetLine: You are ahead of the ending, pushing a load that is already whole.
cells.place: at the ending that clears the ground for what comes after

cells.tense: Something that took everything to build is done now, and you are moving around it without touching it.
cells.ask: Sit with it for five minutes and let yourself feel one part of it, nothing more.
cells.core:
What you carried to the end is standing right here, and you pass it by. You talk about it in the flattest terms, the way you would describe a schedule. The finish is real, but it has not reached your hands, so the ground under it is still occupied and nothing new can land there yet.

Let one part of it land. You do not have to rush the feeling or put it to use. No one is asking you to be moved on schedule. Just sit down next to the finished thing and let one piece of it be true in your body. The next thing needs empty ground, and this is how the ground gets cleared.
cells.sheetLine: It is finished, and you are moving past it untouched.
cells.place: at the ending that clears the ground for what comes after

cells.tense: You are the one making this ending, and you keep saying it landed on you.
cells.ask: Tell one person that the ending is yours — you chose it, you timed it, you cleared the way.
cells.core:
Look at what is already under way: you decide what leaves and when it goes. The clearing is yours. Yet when it comes up, you describe it as the season, the circumstance, somebody else's decision landing on you. The work is real. The claim is sitting somewhere you can see it from.

Endings hold their shape when you call them once. This choice is simpler than the completion it clears away. Say it is yours, not to make a case, just to have it in your own hands. Same move, earlier form. What shifts once it is spoken that way?
cells.sheetLine: You are clearing the ground and calling it something that landed on you.
cells.place: at the ending that clears the ground for what comes after

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a finished thing stands in the way of clearing — the card only says what pure possibility became is now carried whole, not that it is holding anything up; the person could reasonably say the load is still moving and not finished at all. If that read is wrong, the asks still hold: naming what is finished is the same act whether the thing is done or nearly so, and the cost named is the honest one. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line about doors that are 'already' behind, which presumes the past and does the person's thinking for them.
